instrument_title: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016
amendment_lineage: RBI/2025-26/51 dated 2025-06-12 (originating notification; now shown 'withdrawn' on rbi.org.in as of 2026-10-21, superseded by consolidation into the Master Direction)
KYC consolidated Master Direction page, confirmed live with paragraph 38(e) present, checked 2026-10-21
clause_text: The RE shall intimate its customers, in advance, to update their KYC.
clause_summary: Requires regulated entities to notify customers before periodic KYC updates and send reminders after the due date; each set must include at least three communications, including a letter, and communications must be recorded for audit.
action: Send advance notices and post-due-date reminders for periodic KYC update.

exemptions.clause_text: Paragraph 2 of the KYC Master Direction applies the Direction to every regulated entity 'except where specifically mentioned otherwise', and its proviso states that this rule shall not apply to 'small accounts' referred to in paragraph 23 of Chapter VI.
exemptions.notes: 2026-10-21: project owner independently pulled the full consolidated Master Direction text; paragraph 2's proviso and paragraph 23's small-account definition both match word-for-word. Paragraph 2's proviso carries no visible amendment footnote in the text, unlike paragraph 23 (footnote 73) and nearby amended sub-clauses -- this suggests the small-account carve-out may be part of the Direction's original 2016 text and could predate the conservative effective_from set below by years. effective_from is kept conservative (2025-08-14, the date this page was last confirmed updated) rather than guessing an earlier date; do not change it without checking the 2016 original text or an official amendment history. The exact boundary between this general Direction-wide proviso and paragraph 38(e)'s specific notice duty still needs confirmation before gold verification.

notes: 2026-10-21: the project owner opened both official pages in their own browser and sent screenshots. Finding: the standalone amendment notification page (Id=12866) now displays a red 'withdrawn' stamp. Cross-checked against the full consolidated Master Direction text (also pasted by the owner): paragraph 38(e) 'Due Notices for Periodic Updation of KYC' is present there, word-for-word identical to clause_text below ('The RE shall intimate its customers, in advance, to update their KYC.'). Reading: 'withdrawn' most likely means the standalone notification was superseded by being folded into the consolidated Master Direction (RBI's normal practice once a circular's changes are merged), not that paragraph 38(e) itself was repealed -- the clause is live in the current consolidated text. official_url was switched to the consolidated Master Direction (the current authoritative page) rather than the withdrawn notification; the notification is kept in amendment_lineage as the originating instrument. This is a stronger check than before (clause text independently confirmed by two separate reads), but is still not a full amendment-lineage legal verification -- confirm there is no later, further amendment before gold_verified.

instrument_title: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016
amendment_lineage: KYC consolidated Master Direction page, paragraph 39, checked 2026-10-21 against the full page text the project owner pasted
clause_text: In case of existing customers, RE shall obtain the Permanent Account Number or equivalent e-document thereof or Form No. 60, by such date as may be notified by the Central Government, failing which RE shall temporarily cease operations in the account till the time the Permanent Account Number or equivalent e-documents thereof or Form No. 60 is submitted by the customer.
clause_summary: Requires regulated entities to obtain PAN (or Form 60) from existing customers by the notified date, or temporarily stop operating the account until it is provided -- unless the customer could not provide it due to injury, illness, or age-related infirmity, in which case the RE's internal policy must allow continued (but more closely monitored) operation.
action: Obtain PAN or Form 60 from existing customers by the notified date, or temporarily cease account operations.

exemptions.notes: Paragraph 39's proviso requires REs to build a relaxation into their internal policy for customers unable to provide PAN/Form 60 due to injury, illness, or old-age infirmity, allowing continued (enhanced-monitoring) operation instead of ceasing the account. Modeled here as an EXEMPT relation on the 'temporarily cease operations' consequence, not on the underlying duty to eventually obtain the document. effective_from is conservatively set to the 2025-08-14 consolidation-observation date pending amendment-lineage verification, same convention as the paragraph 2/23 small-account exemption on the other pilot obligation.

notes: Second pilot clause, added 2026-10-21. Clause text cross-checked directly against the full consolidated Master Direction page text the project owner pasted into chat (independent of the earlier screenshot check on paragraph 38(e)/2/23). Not yet dual-annotated or amendment-lineage verified; do not treat as gold.

instrument_title: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
amendment_lineage: SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015 -- consolidated text last amended 14 Jul 2026, regulation 15(2)(b), checked 2026-10-21
clause_text: With effect from April 01, 2025, the provisions of regulation 23 shall be applicable to a listed entity whose equity shares are listed on the SME Exchange, where such entity has paid-up equity share capital exceeding Rupees ten crore or net worth exceeding Rupees twenty-five crore, as on the last day of the previous financial year; once applicable, this continues to apply unless both thresholds remain below the limit for three consecutive financial years.
clause_summary: Determines when an SME-Exchange-listed company must start following SEBI's related-party-transaction rules (regulation 23): once its paid-up equity capital crosses Rs 10 crore OR its net worth crosses Rs 25 crore, as measured at the end of the previous financial year.
action: Become subject to SEBI LODR regulation 23's related-party-transaction requirements.
notes: First SEBI pilot clause, added 2026-10-21, fetched directly from the official SEBI LODR consolidated PDF (not yet independently human-confirmed the way the two RBI KYC clauses were via owner screenshot -- kept at the more conservative 'source_located_clause_not_gold_verified' status for that reason). Introduces a numeric-threshold condition (paid-up capital / net worth in crore) rather than a boolean fact, to exercise the 'gt' comparison operator with real data. Regulation 23's own substantive related-party-transaction requirements were not visible in the fetched text and are not modeled here -- only regulation 15(2)(b)'s applicability trigger is. Do not treat as gold without independent human verification and without first checking the omitted regulation 23 text.

instrument_title: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016
amendment_lineage: KYC consolidated Master Direction page, paragraph 17(3), checked 2026-10-21 against the full page text the project owner pasted. The 2025-08-14 date is the consolidated page's own last-updated date, not a confirmed original inception date for paragraph 17 itself -- this account type is a pre-existing provision, not a new 2025 rule, so treat effective_from as conservative/approximate.
clause_text: The aggregate balance of all the deposit accounts of the customer shall not exceed rupees one lakh (for an account opened on an OTP-based e-KYC, non-face-to-face basis under paragraph 17).
clause_summary: A bank account opened for a customer using OTP-based e-KYC (no in-person verification) must be kept under a Rs 1,00,000 total-balance cap across all such deposit accounts of that customer.
action: Ensure the aggregate balance across all deposit accounts of the customer does not exceed Rs 1,00,000.
subject_scope: RBI-regulated entity offering OTP-based e-KYC deposit accounts
notes: Third RBI pilot clause, added 2026-10-21. Sourced from the same already owner-confirmed KYC Master Direction full text used for the paragraph 39 clause, this time paragraph 17(3) (OTP-based e-KYC / non-face-to-face account balance cap). Related caps exist in paragraphs 17(4) (annual credit cap, Rs 2 lakh) and 17(5) (annual loan cap, Rs 60,000) but are not modeled yet.
